channel.title: Said & Checked: Elections and Parties — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Elections and Parties, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-22: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Greg Murphy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Greg Murphy, U.S. Representative: “It made us the weakest Republican district in the state.” Unsettled. Figures attributed to the North Carolina General Assembly, as reported by Roll Call and WFAE (the Assembly's district file could not be read directly), put Trump's 2024 margin in the redrawn 3rd District at about 14 points, down from 22, but about 12 points in the 1st and 10 points in the unchanged 11th. Whether the 3rd is the weakest depends on whether 'Republican district' means seats Republicans held or seats the map leans Republican, and on the measure used.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-21: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump, Josh Shapiro)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “It was a hoax made up by the Democrats” Unsettled. The Mueller report says the FBI opened its investigation on July 31, 2016, after a foreign government's report about George Papadopoulos, and the special counsel was appointed on May 17, 2017 by Acting Attorney General Rod Rosenstein; it shows no Democratic origin for the opening. The Justice Department inspector general and Durham reports, which address the Democratic-funded Steele dossier, could not be read directly, so whether the investigation can be read as 'made up by the Democrats' stays open.
  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “I've now set a record every election I've run in and just set another one.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's governor results show Shapiro's 2022 total of 3,031,137 votes as the most any Pennsylvania candidate for governor had received through 2022 (Wolf, 2018: 2,895,652), and unofficial 2026 reports put his new total near 3.04 million. Certified 2026 results and his attorney general races were not available, the statement does not name which record, and a search result reports a 2024 statewide total above his, so 'a record every election' cannot be matched to one official measure.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Chip Roy, Thomas Massie)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chip Roy, U.S. Representative: “after 30 years of Republican one-party rule” Unsettled. Republicans have held the Texas governorship since 1995 and the state Senate since 1997, but the state House only since 2003, so the span of one-party control is 23 to 31 years depending on which offices are counted; this rests on a secondary summary, not the Legislative Reference Library's tables.
  • Chip Roy, U.S. Representative: “We spent $500 million to get our butts kicked in Texas, $250 million trying to prop up a U.S. Senate candidate” Unsettled. FEC independent-expenditure filings in AskAmerica's warehouse show about $226 million spent opposing the Democratic Senate candidate and $103 million supporting the Republican in Texas in 2026, and the Texas Tribune reported other totals by different measures; no total matches $250 million or $500 million, and the answer depends on what spending is counted.
  • Thomas Massie, U.S. Representative: “It got $32 million spent against me.” Unsettled. FEC independent-expenditure filings in AskAmerica's warehouse show about $10.1 million spent opposing Massie in the 2026 cycle, led by MAGA KY ($6.2 million) and United Democracy Project ($3.6 million). Reported ad-spending totals near $32 million cover both sides of the race, and his opponent's own campaign spending was not counted, so the total depends on what is included; the FEC record could not be read directly outside the warehouse.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Chuck Schumer, Emily Randall)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Reported as: Schumer, the top Democrat in the Senate for nearly a decade, contends that he still has the needed votes to be elected majority leader.” Unsettled. The secret-ballot leadership vote is set for Dec. 1 and no whip count has been published; the AP reports about 15 of the 55 incoming Democratic senators have publicly backed Schumer and four Sen. Chris Van Hollen, which shows neither a majority nor a shortfall.
  • Emily Randall, U.S. Representative from Washington: “People have messaged me asking if Bernie Sanders could be the speaker of the House” Unsettled. The only record of the messages is Randall's own account as reported by PBS NewsHour, which says she was watching direct messages about the leadership election arrive on Instagram. No independent record (her posts, or reporting that saw the messages) was found; her social media accounts were not searched.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Chuck Schumer, Joe Biden)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader” Unsettled. The Dec. 1 Senate Democratic leadership vote is a secret ballot that has not yet been held, and no public count shows a majority of the caucus backing Schumer. Published tallies of declared support (reported as about 14 for Schumer, 4 for Van Hollen and 38 uncommitted) decide nothing either way.
  • Joe Biden, Former President of the United States: “the only person who'd ever beaten Donald Trump” Unsettled. Biden is the only person to have defeated Trump in a presidential general election (2020). Ted Cruz beat Trump in the 2016 Iowa caucuses and other Republican primary contests, so the statement holds only if it means general elections, and the wording does not say.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “We have two senators-elect who would not be there if the current majority leader had his way” Unsettled. Reporting conflicts on whether Sen. Schumer publicly endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan (one outlet says he endorsed her; another says leadership had only a private preference). In Minnesota no public backing of Peggy Flanagan's opponent by Schumer, the DSCC or Senate Majority PAC was found, only reports of a private preference. Figures are as reported by news outlets; no official record covers private preferences.

item.title: Said & Checked, Elections and Parties, 2026-11-15: 1 contradicted (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “Republicans in Washington raised twice as many funds.” Contradicted. AskAmerica's Federal Election Commission data for the 2026 cycle show the three Republican national party committees with receipts of $843.1 million (RNC $341.5 million, NRCC $263.8 million, NRSC $237.8 million) against $725.5 million for the three Democratic committees (DNC $252.3 million, DCCC $256.8 million, DSCC $216.4 million): about 16 percent more, not twice. The FEC's own 18-month summary gives the same ratio. Still open: super PACs and other outside groups, which were not counted.
